what_the_code_actually_does:
CONFIRMED at main_sha 53b0637. The resume gate reads status and never the audit verdict.

(1) src/socr/pipeline/orchestrator.py:4723 (inside _load_terminal_page, defined at :4628) --
    `            if winning.get("status") != PageStatus.SUCCESS.value:`
    followed by `return None`. This is the ONLY content-quality test the gate applies to
    the serialised winning_output. The gate's full skip conjunction is: sidecar+fragment
    both exist; sidecar parses to a dict; meta["terminal"] is exactly True (:4695);
    meta["run_fingerprint"] == self._run_fingerprint() (:4700); meta["input_checksum"]
    == safe_checksum(current pdf) (:4710-4712); winning_output present and a non-empty
    dict (:4716); status == SUCCESS (:4723); body non-empty and not is_page_failed_marker
    (:4733); PageOutput.from_dict succeeds. `audit_passed` appears NOWHERE in the function.

(2) The SUCCESS + audit_passed=False shape is reachable and is what gets written.
    src/socr/pipeline/orchestrator.py:2762 --
    `                    att.output.audit_passed = att.accepted`
    In agentic best-effort (socr/pipeline/agentic.py::_best_effort, :113-136) when NOTHING
    is accepted, route_page still returns the most trustworthy attempt as final_output;
    its provider status stays SUCCESS (extraction succeeded as an operation) while
    accepted=False makes audit_passed=False. ps.best_output = decision.final_output (:2771).

(3) src/socr/core/manifest.py:463-464 --
    `    if p.best_output:` / `        return p.best_output`
    is the last-resort branch of _winning_page_output. For a SCANNED page (is_born_digital
    False) with no scanned_table_evidence_failed flag and no whole-doc attempt, every
    earlier demotion branch is skipped: the top `if p.best_output and p.best_output.audit_passed`
    (:314) is False, the GH-90 scanned floor (:337) needs scanned_table_evidence_failed,
    the D3/native-fallback block (:355) needs p.is_born_digital and p.native_text. So the
    rejected attempt is returned verbatim, SUCCESS + audit_passed=False.

(4) _flush_page_sidecar (orchestrator.py:4525) records exactly that object as
    meta["winning_output"] and meta["status"], so the sidecar says status="success"
    with audit_passed=false, and the gate at :4723 grants the skip. Verified empirically:
    the reproducer's precondition asserts on the written sidecar all pass, and
    _load_terminal_page returns the rejected PageOutput rather than None.

Scope note: the born-digital sibling of this shape is ALREADY defended, which is why the
bug survived. When p.is_born_digital and p.native_text are set, _winning_page_output's
native-fallback branch stamps WARNING / audit_passed=False (manifest.py:427-429), so the
status check at :4723 catches it -- that is exactly what the existing test
tests/test_pp5_resume_ledger.py::test_flagged_native_fallback_sidecar_records_winner_not_attempt
asserts. On a SCANNED page nothing demotes the status, so audit_passed is the only
remaining signal and the gate does not read it.

notes:
1. The issue's line references have drifted (it cites _load_terminal_page at ~4241-4268
   and _winning_page_output at ~370-373). At main_sha they are orchestrator.py:4628-4748
   and manifest.py:463-464. The DIAGNOSIS is correct; only the coordinates are stale.

2. The issue says "_winning_page_output returns that output for scanned pages" without
   naming the branch. It is the last-resort `if p.best_output: return p.best_output`
   (manifest.py:463), NOT an early return -- it is reached only because every demotion
   branch above it is born-digital- or flag-gated. This matters for the fix: adding an
   audit_passed check to the gate is correct, but a fix that instead tried to demote the
   status inside _winning_page_output would change what the manifest and the assembled
   .md ship for scanned all-reject pages, which is a much larger blast radius and would
   collide with the byte-identity golden tests.

3. Partly-mitigating fact the issue does not mention: _restore_terminal_page_state
   (orchestrator.py:4750+) DOES restore `ps.judge_rejected` from the sidecar
   (`ps.judge_rejected = bool(meta.get("judge_rejected", False))`). So some downstream
   surfacing may still fire on a resumed rejected page. This does NOT save the corpus --
   the rejected TEXT is still restored verbatim and no re-OCR is attempted, which is the
   silent-content-loss vector -- but it means the resumed page is not necessarily
   invisible at every surface. Worth checking when writing the fix's surfacing assertions.

4. Non-vacuity: the test imports only symbols that exist at main_sha (UnifiedPipeline,
   _flush_page_fragment, _flush_page_sidecar, _load_terminal_page, PageOutput, PageStatus,
   DocumentState, DocumentHandle, PipelineConfig, EngineType). It fails on the behavioural
   assertion `resumed is None`, not on an import or a setup error -- the four precondition
   asserts above it all PASS at main_sha, proving the sidecar really carries the
   SUCCESS + audit_passed=false shape before the gate is exercised.

5. Hermeticity: the test never enters _phase_agentic or process(), so no
   _available_engines_for_agentic patch is required. It needs PyMuPDF (fitz) to build a
   1-page PDF and uses pytest.importorskip, matching the existing PP-5 harness.
